To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the occurrence of Borrelia burgdofleri sensu lato is not homogeneous in Switzerland and is not restricted to the three known species, B. burgdofleri, B. garinii et B. afzelii.

(1) Borrelia are present in the ticks of all locations studied, (2) the infection rate varies from 10% to 50% in Ixodes ricinus and is independent of altitude and vegetation cover, (3) the Borrelia are not evenly distributed in the tick population but are clustered, and (4) the Borreliae are not evenly distributed among tick species and are not evenly distributed within the Ixodes ricinustick species.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Borrelia is present in all sites where I. ricinus was found, and that there are different genospecies present in the ticks of Valais.
